answer.says: You are right, Sunil. I have been making the particular samosa into a universal concept, and in doing so, I have forgotten that it is meant to be eaten. On Diwali, even dialectics must yield to the appetite.
answer.thought: His command to stop talking and eat is a practical negation of my abstract tendency. I am trying to make the moment into a thesis, but he insists on the moment as a fact. He is right: the spirit that refuses to digest its own thoughts is merely hungry and pedantic.
